projects.title: Quiet Rooms
projects.desc: For the Quiet Rooms issue we photographed the empty suites of a George Town heritage hotel just after dawn, before the housekeeping trolleys came out, and let the furniture carry the story, and the pages were set with wide margins so each frame could breathe, and the palette stayed close to plaster, teak and morning haze off the strait while short captions ran beneath the images like handwritten notes, giving the whole editorial the pace of a slow walk down a shophouse corridor that had not yet decided to wake up.

projects.title: Paper Light
projects.desc: Paper Light was shot for a Petaling Street paper merchant using nothing but sheets of translucent paper as light modifiers, and the studies moved from hard folds to soft gradients as the afternoon storms rolled over the city and back out again, and the series kept a single fixed camera position so the paper itself became the performer, bending, tearing and glowing, while the prints were finished matte so the highlights would sit quietly instead of shining.

projects.title: Salt Air
projects.desc: Salt Air set the direction for an east coast outerwear line built for the landas season, and we shot the whole campaign on the Terengganu shoreline in November, building the visual world around wind rather than water, letting fabric, hair and lalang all lean the same way in every frame, and the campaign grammar used long South China Sea horizons with the subject placed low, so the clothing read as shelter inside weather, and every touchpoint from lookbook to signage kept that same leaning horizon.

projects.title: Neon Harvest
projects.desc: Neon Harvest paired pasar produce with electric colour for a Klang Valley grocer that wanted to feel awake, and we staged kangkung, chillies and bunga kantan like sculpture under saturated gel lighting, keeping compositions frontal and symmetrical so the strangeness came only from colour, and the campaign rolled out as posters, short loops and shelf wobblers that all shared the same three-colour discipline, from Bangsar to the wet market in Cheras.

projects.title: Slow Bloom
projects.desc: Slow Bloom advertised a fragrance built on serai wangi and frangipani by refusing to hurry, and the films held single flowers opening in near real time while the bottle appeared only in the final second, and the stills used the same patience, printed large with almost nothing on the page, and the media plan placed the work in clinic waiting rooms, LRT platforms and hotel lobbies along Jalan Sultan Ismail, exactly where people had time to watch something bloom.

projects.title: Glass Season
projects.desc: Glass Season was a design programme for a glassware maker outside Shah Alam, and we rebuilt the catalogue system around refraction, letting each object distort a coloured field behind it so the products drew their own portraits, and the typography stayed small and factual beneath these distortions, and the system carried through packaging, trade fair stands at MITEC and a slim annual publication.

projects.title: Cold Light
projects.desc: Cold Light art-directed a winter series for a KL gear brand whose customers only ever meet snow on holiday, and we took the shoot to Hokkaido and kept the sun below the mountains the whole time so the story lived in blue shadow, and gear and athletes were photographed with the same distant respect, small against the terrain, and the grade pulled all warmth out except one orange accent that travelled through the series like a signal, the exact orange of a Malaysian dusk the brand wanted to carry abroad.

projects.title: Street Chorus
projects.desc: Street Chorus followed a contemporary dance company through their own Kuala Lumpur, and instead of stages we shot rehearsals at pedestrian crossings in Chow Kit, between the tarpaulins of the morning market and in the underpasses below the LRT tracks, letting passers-by drift through frame, and the photography leaned on long lenses and found light so the dancers stayed inside the life of the street rather than on top of it, and the final selection ran as a broadsheet insert.

projects.title: Static Bloom
projects.desc: Static Bloom launched a speaker line from a Penang electronics house by photographing sound, and we drove fine powder, petals and thread with low frequencies until each frame caught a bloom of movement at its peak, and the campaign kept the product silent at the edge of the image while its effect filled the centre, and the headline system used only verbs, set small, in mono, in both English and Malay.

projects.title: Clay Studies
projects.desc: Clay Studies was a product development diary for a ceramics workshop in Ipoh working an hour from the clay pits of Kuala Kangsar, and we documented every failed glaze and slumped form alongside the successes, numbering all of them equally, and the honesty became the identity, with the final range presented next to its own rejects, and the launch publication printed the whole sequence uncut so buyers could see the path.

projects.title: Red Interval
projects.desc: Red Interval was a colour-themed issue for a KL culture magazine where every spread had to earn its single red element, and we built each story around waiting, queues, platforms and pauses, with red arriving as an ang pow, a temple door off Jalan Tun H.S. Lee or a signal lamp at Kuala Lumpur station, and the type sat in the intervals between images, and the issue closed with the only fully red spread, printed on uncoated stock.

projects.title: Bone China
projects.desc: Bone China was an identity for a small porcelain house that has fired kilns in the same Kinta Valley town for three generations, and we drew the mark from the thinnest point of their teacups, a line that almost disappears against light, and the system used that near-absence everywhere, hairline rules, pale embossing and photography shot against white so the objects had to define themselves by shadow alone, and the effect made thinness itself the brand.

projects.title: After Hours
projects.desc: After Hours photographed the towers of the Golden Triangle once everyone had gone home, and the series treated cleaning trolleys, standby lights and abandoned chairs as still-life subjects, and every image used only the light the building itself left on, and the project ran as a book and a slow slideshow in the lobby of the very towers it documented, playing to empty escalators while the surau light stayed on down the corridor.

projects.title: Field Notes
projects.desc: Field Notes was a personal project made across one padi season in Sekinchan, and it collected fences, tools, weather and hands in no particular order, printed at postcard size and posted weekly to a small list of subscribers, and nothing was retouched and nothing was explained, and by the time the harvesters came through in the last week the mailing list had grown large enough to fund the next season.

projects.title: Open Storage
projects.desc: Open Storage catalogued a national depot rather than an exhibition, and we photographed crates, racking and wrapped sculptures exactly as found in the climate-controlled back rooms off Jalan Temerloh, and each object entry carried its storage code as the headline instead of a title, and the catalogue let readers feel the pleasure of the back room, where art waits in blankets, and the print run sold out before the show opened.

projects.title: Iron Choir
projects.desc: Iron Choir directed the imagery for the centenary of a foundry that began in the tin years of the Kinta Valley, and we recorded the works as if they were an orchestra, brass pours, hammer sections and the long quiet of cooling halls, and the photographs were sequenced by loudness rather than chronology, and the anniversary book opened silent and closed at full roar, with the type growing a point size every chapter.

projects.title: Deep Signal
projects.desc: Deep Signal designed the launch system for a Labuan company that puts sensors on the seabed for the offshore industry, and we translated their sonar returns into a graphic language of concentric fades, and the palette held to two blues and a warning orange, and everything from investor decks to hull decals came from the same wave grammar, and the system survived contact with engineering unchanged, which we count as the real result.

projects.title: Small Rituals
projects.desc: Small Rituals was an editorial about the tiny repeated actions that hold a Malaysian day together, and we photographed hands only, pulling teh, folding kuih, locking the grille gate, watering orchids on the corridor, across nine households from Sentul to Subang Jaya, and the layouts gave each ritual a full silent spread, and the captions were gathered at the back so the sequence could run without interruption, like a film with the sound turned off.

projects.title: Charged Air
projects.desc: Charged Air advertised an electric motorcycle without ever showing the road, and we shot the machines in monsoon storm light on the open flats outside Sekinchan, letting sky and chassis trade reflections while the thunderheads stacked up over the strait, and the copy ran to five words per execution, in Malay first, and the launch films were cut to the rhythm of distant thunder, and the whole campaign kept its promise of speed by never once moving the camera.

projects.title: Dust Ballet
projects.desc: Dust Ballet was a short film for a heritage denim house that names every wash after an old Perak mine, and we choreographed riders, dust and low sun into a single continuous take on a disused tin land outside Batu Gajah, rehearsed for three days and shot at the fourth dusk, and the fabric was the lead actor, catching light through the haze, and the film ran in one old single-screen cinema in Ipoh for one week, which was the whole strategy, and the queue did the advertising.

studio.heading: The Studio
studio.statement: Imagify is a visual studio in Kuala Lumpur working across identity, image and film. We like briefs with edges, budgets with honesty and rooms with daylight, which in this city means shooting before the four o'clock rain. Most of our projects begin as a conversation about what a brand refuses to do, because the refusals draw the shape faster than the wishes, and from that outline we build systems that stay calm in use and sharp in memory. The studio is small on purpose, one floor of a shophouse off Jalan Mesui. Everyone who starts a project finishes it, and the person who presents the work is the person who made it.
